title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثانى
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape two
body_ar:
الشريط الثانى

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى ءاله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين أما بعد فسنبدأ إن شاء الله تعالى بهذه المصطلحات الأربعة السنة الحديث الخبر الأثر هذه المصطلحات متقاربة لدى أهل الحديث، فيحتاج الطالب إلى التمييز بينها ومعرفة مقتضياتها ودلالاتها، أولا المصطلح الأول السنة السنة في اللغة الطريقة والصميم من كل شيء، فتطلق على الطريقة سواء كانت خيرا أم شرا فمن إطلاقها على الخير قوله تعالى: {سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا} أي طريقة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا، ولا تكون طريقة الرسل إلا خيرا، ومن إطلاقها على الشر قوله تعالى: {قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين} فسنن المكذبين لا تكون إلا شرا، فعلم بهذا أن السنة في اللغة تطلق على الطريقة سواء كانت للخير أو للشر..
body_en:
Tape two.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: we shall begin, God Most High willing, with these four terms — sunnah, ḥadīth, khabar, athar. These terms lie close together in the usage of the people of hadith, and the student needs to distinguish between them and to know what each entails and what each signifies.

First, the first term: sunnah. Sunnah in the language is the way, and the core of a thing. It is applied to a way whether that way is good or evil. An instance of its application to the good is the saying of God Most High: {the way of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:77) — that is, the way of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you; and the way of the messengers can only be good. An instance of its application to evil is the saying of God Most High: {ways have passed away before you, so travel in the land and see what was the end of those who denied} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:137) — for the ways of those who denied can only be evil. It is known by this that sunnah in the language is applied to a way, whether it be to good or to evil..

options: the way, and the core of a thing
the way, and the essence of anything
the way, and the best part of anything
flags.note: Al-ṣamīm is the innermost or hardest part of a thing, hence its core. The lexicographers give it for sunnah alongside 'way', and the Sheikh gives it without elaborating. He then illustrates only the first sense with the two verses and does not return to the second within the published excerpt, so the intended force of al-ṣamīm here cannot be settled from this text.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

This record and id 632 are both tape two, id 632 being marked 'continued'. In the CMS id 632 carries the earlier upload timestamp of the two, so the two halves of tape two are stored in reverse order of their content.

The four terms are left in Arabic where the Sheikh is naming them as terms to be distinguished; translating them at that point would collapse the distinction the lesson exists to draw. The house rule against leaving Arabic to stand as the English does not apply where the Arabic word is itself the object of study.
The verse references have been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse texts alone.
The source spells آله as ءاله in the doxology. The spelling is preserved in body_ar and carries no difference of meaning.
